title: Continuous Quality Platform report
description: The contract between the quality platform and everything that reads it: dashboards, pipelines and AI agents. Semver: a minor version may add fields and never removes them, so a consumer may rely on what it already reads.

schema.description: Semantic version of this document's shape.

run.description: Provenance: enough to reproduce this run and enough to line two runs up against each other.

id.description: Run identifier; also the trace id prefix.

baseRef.description: The ref this run was measured against.

summary.description: The part to read first, and on a clean run the only part that needs reading.

verdict.description: pass: merge. warn: findings worth reading, nothing blocking. fail: a blocking budget was breached. error: the platform itself could not finish.

score.description: For the trend line. No merge decision is ever made on it.

scoreDelta.description: Against the baseline; absent when there is no baseline.

headline.description: One sentence, plain words, no jargon.

blockedBy.description: Names of the budgets that stopped this run.

nextSteps.description: Ordered: what blocks the merge first, then the cheapest wins.

selection.description: Why the run did what it did. An agent told a check did not run must be able to see that no relevant file changed, rather than assume the platform is broken.

skipped.description: Each entry is "analyzer-id (reason in plain words)".

budgets.description: The quality gates, evaluated. This is what decides the merge.

metric.description: The metric key, or a description of the finding selector.

status.description: skip means nothing measured this budget's metric, or a regression budget had no baseline. It is a state, not a pass.

message.description: Actionable without opening a log: the measurement, the baseline, the delta, the rule and the ref compared against.

blocking.description: A non-blocking budget is reported and never stops a merge.

categories.description: Per-area rollup. A category nothing measured is absent rather than scored 100.

findings.description: Deduplicated across tools. Ordered worst first, then new, then by confidence.

id.description: Stable fingerprint. Deliberately excludes the line number, so a finding that moved because an import was added above it is the same finding.

confidence.description: How much the platform trusts this. An agent should read it before acting unattended.

component.description: React component, Go function, endpoint, route.

evidence.description: One short quotation. Never a log.

safeToAutomate.description: The platform's statement that applying this without a human is expected to be correct. Set per-analyzer in a reviewed manifest, never guessed per finding. On a merged finding it is the floor of the merged values.

patch.description: Unified diff, when the tool supplied one.

tools.description: Every analyzer that independently reported this. More than one is real corroboration and raises confidence.

new.description: Absent from the baseline. On a pull request this is what decides whether anyone is asked to care.

metrics.description: Measurements. Only these can be compared against a previous build, so regression gating lives entirely here.

subject.description: Distinguishes the same metric measured over different things: one route, one benchmark, one asset.

analyzers.description: What ran, how long it took, and whether it was cached. Operator data; omitted from the agent report.

artifacts.description: Pointers to detail deliberately left out of the report.

platformErrors.description: The platform's own failures, kept strictly apart from findings. A broken analyzer must never look like a code defect, because an agent told its code has an error will change the code.
